I've been working this land for 30 years. I know it well. My back hurts more than it used to, and with the kids working in the city, it's mostly me handling the farm. I need to be practical.

My 60 mu is split: 35 mu I do wheat in winter, then pull that out in June and put maize straight in — same ground, two harvests. The other 25 mu I put in cotton. Cotton is more work but the price is better per mu when it's good, and I know how to grow it.

For wheat, I always plough after maize harvest in October, get the ground ready. I use the improved variety everyone in the village uses now — better yield than the old seeds my mother used. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, then urea when it starts jointing in March. I irrigate three times: before winter freeze, at jointing, and when the grain is filling. That's what my experience tells me. I spray once for weeds in the cold months and once more in spring for aphids and rust.

For maize, I go right in after wheat with the rotary tiller — no time to plough, wheat comes out mid-June and the maize needs to go in fast. I use hybrid seed, everyone does now, yields are much better. One irrigation at planting if the soil is dry, otherwise the summer rains usually handle it.

For cotton, I plough deep in spring before transplanting. I use Bt hybrid seed now — fewer spray trips for bollworm, which matters since it's just me doing most of the work. I still spray for aphids and mites though, can't avoid it. Three irrigations through the season.

I don't try to do things fancy. I do what has worked on my land for decades.
